climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Too cool for the classic wine grapes. Only very early grapes and hybrids ripen here.
Gewürztraminer is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.
Riesling is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.
Pinot Gris is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.
Pinot Noir is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.

soil.rock: Schist, slate and gneiss break into stony, free-draining soil that holds the day's heat. Schist is rich in magnesium and potassium but poor in organic matter and nitrogen. Granite weathers to coarse, acid, free-draining soil that warms quickly and holds heat. Its acidity tends to lower the grapes' acidity, which suits Gamay.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. It is very acid, which locks up nutrients, so growers spread lime to raise the pH.

land: Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.
Faces the morning sun. Early light dries the dew, which cuts disease, and the grapes are spared the hottest afternoon sun.
